title: Metro ridership dashboard, one honest chart per question
summary: From ridership data you generate, answer five questions with five truthful charts, and say what the data cannot answer.
context: Lakeline Metro is a fictional city metro that wants to understand its riders. You generate a year of hourly tap-in counts for about 20 stations on three lines, with the patterns a real system has: weekday peaks, a different weekend shape, a festival week, a station closed for a month, and a few sensor glitches.
Then answer five questions a planner would ask. For each, build exactly one chart or table and put one or two sentences under it saying what it shows and what it does not.
Honest means axes that start where they should, no misleading bars, no colour that implies a ranking that is not there, and outliers explained rather than quietly dropped.
must_have: The seeded generator and the data it writes, with the planted patterns documented in a file kept apart from the dashboard code.
Five questions written down before you chart anything.
One chart per question, titled with its finding, with labelled units and a data-quality note covering the glitches and how you treated them.
A dashboard page (static HTML, a notebook or a small app) that opens with only what the README says to install.
A short 'cannot answer' section: two questions this data cannot settle, and why.
nice_to_have: A date-range or line filter that changes the charts without changing what they mean.
A colour-blind-safe palette, checked with a simulator.
One command that regenerates the data, the charts and the page.
constraints: No paid services, APIs or accounts. Free charting libraries are fine.
Generated, fictional data only. Do not scrape or download any real transit data.
Do not use a sample dataset that ships with a library as your data.
deliverables: A public repo created after you press Start, with commits spread across the window.
A README with how to run it (regenerate the data, open the dashboard), your five questions, and what is missing.
judge_focus: Whether each chart answers its question, and whether you checked how it could mislead.
How glitches and outliers were found and treated, and whether that choice is visible to a reader.
Whether the charts recover the planted patterns instead of just assuming them.
A trail of commits: the data and its checks first, charts after, each revised for a reason you can state.
bengaluru_context: Analytics teams at Bengaluru mobility, civic-tech and consulting organisations are asked daily to turn a messy log into one chart a decision-maker will trust.
